issues.failure_explanation: A bubble b in B_{k+2}(K) belongs to the plain space W_{k+2}(K) but not, in general, to the enhanced space W̃_{k+2}(K): the enhancement constraint (b−Π^∇_{k+2}b, q)=0 for q of degree k+1,k+2 is not implied by Δb∈P_k and b=0 on ∂K (for q with Δq of degree ≤k one gets (b−Π^∇b,Δq)=−∫_{∂K}Π^∇b ∂_n q, generically nonzero). Likewise W̃_k(K) ⊄ W̃_{k+2}(K) in general. Hence the stated premise for unisolvence is false as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the inclusion claim by the argument that V_k(K) is a direct sum of two spaces each with unisolvent dofs (already established in the text).
issues.overall_effect: Only the justification of Proposition prop:added-4 is affected; the unisolvence itself follows from the direct-sum property and the unisolvence of the dofs of W̃_k(K) and of B_{k+2\setminus k}(K).
issues.title: Unisolvence justified by a false inclusion V_k(K) ⊂ [W̃_{k+2}(K)]^2
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is true and a one-line correct justification is available in the source; nothing downstream changes.

issues.failure_explanation: If b∈B_{k+2}(K) has Π^∇_{k+2}b=0 then ∫bΔq=0 for all q∈P_{k+2}, i.e. b⊥P_k, so |b|_1^2=−∫bΔb=0 and b=0 (this is precisely why Proposition prop:norm_bub holds). Thus the second condition in eq:stab_ah is imposed on the trivial space and gives no information about S^K_{k+2}(Q^∇_{k+2}b, Q^∇_{k+2}b), where Q^∇_{k+2}b∉B_{k+2\k}(K). The stability proof for β_♯>0 nevertheless uses the constants γ_⋆,γ^⋆ for exactly these arguments.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the second condition of eq:stab_ah on the space Q^∇_{k+2}(B_{k+2\k}(K)) (or on [Z_{k+2}(K)]^2 ∩ ker Π^∇_{k+2}), i.e. require γ_⋆ a(Q^∇b,Q^∇b) ≤ S(Q^∇b,Q^∇b) ≤ γ^⋆ a(Q^∇b,Q^∇b) for all b in the bubble space.
issues.overall_effect: For β_♯>0 the upper bound in eq:stab and the case C=1 (β_♯≥1/γ_⋆) in the lower bound rest on an assumption that as written says nothing; the β_♯=0 case (used in all numerics) is unaffected.
issues.title: Bubble stabilization hypothesis (eq:stab_ah, second line) is vacuous: B_{k+2\k}(K) ∩ ker Π^∇_{k+2} = {0}
issues.why_classification: A local restatement of the hypothesis restores the proof; the method, constants and all guarantees survive.

issues.failure_explanation: Adding and subtracting 2a(ṽ,d) yields C^⋆a(v_h,v_h) − 2C^⋆a(ṽ,d), not C^⋆a(v_h,v_h) − a(Q^∇_kṽ,d); more importantly the final step ≤ C^⋆a(v_h,v_h) needs a(Q^∇_kṽ,d) ≥ 0, which is false in general (replacing d by −d changes its sign while a_h(v_h,v_h) is unchanged). The written inference is invalid.

issues.failure_explanation: c_h acts only on Q^0_k q_h, so c_h(q_h,q_h)=0 for any q_h∈Q_k that is a global polynomial of degree ≤k with zero mean (e.g. x−1/2 on the unit square), contradicting the claimed lower bound δ_⋆‖q_h‖_0^2. The correct statement is δ_⋆‖Q^0_k q_h‖_0^2 ≤ c_h(q_h,q_h) ≤ δ^⋆‖Q^0_k q_h‖_0^2, which is what the later proofs actually use.

issues.overall_effect: The displayed property is false; later arguments (Prop. prop:added-6, Thm. thm:est) use the correct version, so no result is invalidated.
issues.title: Global two-sided bound for c_h in terms of ‖q_h‖_0 is false
issues.why_classification: Local correction of a misstatement; nothing depends on the false version.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Given a function $w\in\HunoK\cap C^0(\elementvem)$, we introduce the interpolant $\interVem w\in\vem{k}(\elementvem)$

issues.failure_explanation: The only interpolants defined in the paper are nodal (values at vertices/edge points), requiring continuity, and the only estimates given (Props. prop:added-1, prop:interp_enh) are for H^{k+1} data. The inf-sup proof interpolates v(q_h)∈H^1_0(Ω)^2, whose nodal values are undefined, and uses ‖v−v_I‖_0 ≲ h|v|_1 and ‖v_I‖_1 ≲ ‖v‖_1, neither established. The same gap recurs for p_I with p∈H^1 (k=1 case of Corollary cor:added-1) and for ρ_I with ρ∈H^1 in the L^2 duality argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Introduce (or cite) an H^1-stable quasi-interpolant onto the enhanced VEM spaces preserving moments up to degree k−2 and satisfying ‖v−v_I‖_0+h|v−v_I|_1 ≤ Ch^s‖v‖_s for 1≤s≤k+1 (e.g. Scott–Zhang on a sub-triangulation composed with the VEM interpolant), and use it in these proofs.
issues.overall_effect: The weak inf-sup condition, hence the well-posedness and error estimates built on it, as well as the k=1 pressure estimate and the L^2 velocity estimate, rely on interpolation properties not available in the paper.
issues.title: Nodal VEM interpolant applied to H^1 (non-continuous) functions with unavailable low-regularity estimates
issues.why_classification: A standard, citable tool closes the gap without changing method, rates or scope.

issues.failure_explanation: The test function is v_h = v_I + d_h with d_h∈B_{k+2\k} chosen to match moments of v(q_h)−v_I, but no estimate of |d_h|_{1,Ω} is given, and eq:norm_equal only normalizes v(q_h), not v_h. Without |d_h|_1 ≲ h^{-1}‖Π^0_k(v−v_I)‖_0 ≲ ‖q_h‖_0 (scaling/inverse estimate on the bubble space) the conclusion cannot be rescaled to satisfy ‖v_h‖_1=‖q_h‖_0 with h-independent ζ_1, ζ_2; the final sentence asserts the statement without this step.
